# Page: Overview

# Overview

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [scgpt/__init__.py](scgpt/__init__.py)
- [scgpt/data_collator.py](scgpt/data_collator.py)

</details>



scGPT is a foundation model for single-cell multi-omics data analysis using generative AI. This page provides a high-level overview of the scGPT system, its purpose, main components, and capabilities. For specific details about implementation, please refer to the individual component pages referenced throughout this document.

Sources: [README.md:1-14](), [pyproject.toml:1-9]()

## Purpose and Scope

scGPT aims to advance single-cell genomics research by applying transformer-based deep learning models to analyze gene expression data. The system enables various analytical tasks including data integration, cell type annotation, perturbation prediction, gene regulatory network inference, and multi-omics integration. The scGPT framework implements specialized transformer architectures optimized for processing gene expression data, with support for both pretraining on large datasets and fine-tuning for specific downstream tasks.

Sources: [README.md:3-4](), [pyproject.toml:4]()

## System Architecture

The scGPT system consists of several interconnected components organized in a modular architecture. The following diagram illustrates the high-level architecture of the system:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Core Components"
        TransMod["TransformerModel"] --> Encoders
        TransGen["TransformerGenerator"] --> Encoders
        Encoders --> GeneEnc["GeneEncoder"]
        Encoders --> ValEnc["ContinuousValueEncoder"]
        Encoders --> BatchEnc["BatchLabelEncoder"]
        TransMod --> Decoders
        TransGen --> Decoders
        Decoders --> ExprDec["ExprDecoder"]
        Decoders --> ClsDec["ClsDecoder"]
        Decoders --> MVCDec["MVCDecoder"]
        
        Token["GeneVocab/Tokenizer"]
        DataCol["DataCollator"]
        Trainer["Trainer"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Processing"
        Preproc["Preprocessor"] --> Filter["Filter Genes"]
        Filter --> Norm["Normalize"]
        Norm --> LogTrans["Log Transform"]
        LogTrans --> HVG["Subset HVGs"]
        HVG --> Bin["Bin Values"]
        
        SCBank["scBank DataBank"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Tasks & Applications"
        CellEmb["Cell Embedding"]
        ZeroShot["Zero-Shot Integration"]
        RefMap["Reference Mapping"]
        GRN["GRN Analysis"]
        Perturb["Perturbation Prediction"]
        MultiOmics["Multi-omics Integration"]
    end
    
    Token --> DataCol
    DataCol --> TransMod
    Preproc --> DataCol
    SCBank --> DataCol
    
    TransMod --> Trainer
    TransGen --> Trainer
    
    Trainer --> CellEmb
    Trainer --> ZeroShot
    Trainer --> GRN
    Trainer --> Perturb
    Trainer --> MultiOmics
    
    CellEmb --> RefMap
    ZeroShot --> RefMap
```

Sources: [scgpt/__init__.py:18-29](), [README.md:57-69]()

## Data Flow Pipeline

The following diagram illustrates the data flow pipeline from raw gene expression data to processed cell embeddings:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Raw["Raw Gene Expression Data"] --> Preproc["Preprocessor"]
    Preproc --> Filtered["Filtered Data"]
    Filtered --> Token["Tokenizer/GeneVocab"]
    Token --> Genes["Gene Tokens"]
    Genes --> DataCol["DataCollator"]
    Values["Expression Values"] --> DataCol
    DataCol --> Batches["Padded/Masked Batches"]
    Batches --> Model["scGPT Model"]
    Model --> Embedding["Cell Embeddings"]
    
    subgraph "DataCollator Operations"
        Padding["Padding"]
        Truncation["Truncation/Sampling"]
        Masking["Value Masking (MLM)"]
        Binning["Expression Binning"]
    end
    
    DataCol -.- "DataCollator Operations"
```

Sources: [scgpt/data_collator.py:10-50](), [scgpt/__init__.py:19-20]()

## Core Components

### Model Architecture

The scGPT system is built around two primary model architectures:

1. **TransformerModel**: A general-purpose model for tasks like cell type classification and embedding generation
2. **TransformerGenerator**: A specialized model for perturbation prediction

Both models leverage transformer architecture with customized encoders and decoders specifically designed for gene expression data. For more details on model architecture, see [Model Architecture](#2.1).

### Data Processing

The data processing pipeline handles preparation of single-cell RNA-seq data for input to the transformer models. Key steps include:

- Gene filtering
- Normalization
- Log transformation
- Highly Variable Gene (HVG) selection
- Expression value binning
- Tokenization
- Data collation with padding and masking

For more details on data processing, see [Data Processing](#2.2).

Sources: [scgpt/data_collator.py:11-47]()

### Training System

The training system orchestrates model training, evaluation, and testing workflows. It provides functionality for batch preparation, loss computation, optimization, and evaluation metrics tracking. For more details on the training system, see [Training System](#2.3).

Sources: [scgpt/__init__.py:21-29]()

## Tasks and Applications

scGPT supports multiple analytical tasks for single-cell data:

| Task | Description | Related Page |
|------|-------------|--------------|
| Zero-Shot Integration | Integration of single-cell datasets without task-specific fine-tuning | [Zero-Shot Integration](#3.1) |
| Reference Mapping | Transfer of cell type annotations from reference to query datasets | [Reference Mapping](#3.2) |
| Cell Embedding | Generation of low-dimensional cell representations | [Cell Embedding](#3.3) |
| Perturbation Prediction | Prediction of cellular responses to genetic or chemical perturbations | [Perturbation Prediction](#3.4) |
| GRN Analysis | Inference of gene regulatory networks | [GRN Analysis](#3.5) |
| Multi-omics Integration | Integration of multiple data modalities (RNA, ATAC, etc.) | [Multi-omics Integration](#3.6) |

Sources: [README.md:74-85]()

## Pretrained Models

scGPT provides several pretrained model checkpoints for different applications:

| Model name | Description | 
|------------|-------------|
| whole-human (recommended) | Pretrained on 33 million normal human cells |
| continual pretrained | For zero-shot cell embedding related tasks |
| brain | Pretrained on 13.2 million brain cells |
| blood | Pretrained on 10.3 million blood and bone marrow cells |
| heart | Pretrained on 1.8 million heart cells |
| lung | Pretrained on 2.1 million lung cells |
| kidney | Pretrained on 814 thousand kidney cells |
| pan-cancer | Pretrained on 5.7 million cells of various cancer types |

These models serve as the foundation for various downstream tasks and can be used directly or fine-tuned for specific applications. For more details on available models, see [Pretrained Models](#4).

Sources: [README.md:57-69]()

## Code Organization

The scGPT codebase is organized into several key modules:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class scGPT {
        __version__
        logger
    }
    
    class model {
        TransformerModel
        TransformerGenerator

        tokenize_and_pad_batch
    }
    
    class scbank {
        DataBank
        CellXGeneDataBank
    }

        load_pretrained
        setup_seed
        evaluate_clustering
    }
    
    class tasks {
        cell_emb
        zero_shot
        reference_mapping
        perturbation
        grn
    }

        DataCollator
    }
    
    class trainer {
        prepare_data
        prepare_dataloader
        train
        evaluate
        test
    }
    
    scGPT --> model
    scGPT --> tokenizer
    scGPT --> scbank
    scGPT --> utils
    scGPT --> tasks
    scGPT --> data_collator
    scGPT --> trainer
```

Sources: [scgpt/__init__.py:18-29]()

## Installation and Dependencies

scGPT works with Python >= 3.7.13 and R >= 3.6.1. The main dependencies include:

- PyTorch (>=1.13.0)
- scanpy (^1.9.1)
- scvi-tools (>=0.16.0,<1.0)
- datasets (^2.3.0)
- flash-attention (optional, recommended)

For a complete guide on installation, see [Installation Guide](#6).

Sources: [README.md:28-54](), [pyproject.toml:11-26]()

## Getting Started

To get started with scGPT, you can:

1. Install the package using pip: `pip install scgpt "flash-attn<1.0.5"`
2. Download a pretrained model checkpoint
3. Use the model for:
   - Cell embedding generation
   - Zero-shot integration
   - Reference mapping
   - Fine-tuning for specific tasks

For detailed tutorials and examples, refer to the task-specific pages in the [Tasks and Applications](#3) section.

Sources: [README.md:32-38]()

## Prerequisites

scGPT requires the following environment:

| Component | Requirement | Purpose |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| **Python** | >= 3.7.13 | Core language runtime |
| **R** | >= 3.6.1 | Required by some dependencies (scvi-tools, scanpy) |
| **CUDA** | 11.7+ recommended | For GPU acceleration with flash-attention |
| **GPU** | Optional but recommended | Significantly faster training and inference |

**Sources:** [README.md:30](), [pyproject.toml:12]()

---

## Basic Installation

The simplest installation uses pip to install the scGPT package from PyPI:

```bash
pip install scgpt "flash-attn<1.0.5"
```

The `flash-attn` dependency is optional but strongly recommended for performance. If you encounter installation issues with `flash-attn`, scGPT will automatically fall back to standard PyTorch attention mechanisms.

**Known issue (as of 2023.09):** If you encounter errors related to Google's `orbax` package, use:

```bash
pip install scgpt "flash-attn<1.0.5" "orbax<0.1.8"
```

### Optional: Experiment Tracking

For logging training metrics and visualizations, install Weights & Biases:

```bash
pip install wandb
```

**Sources:** [README.md:28-54](), [pyproject.toml:1-41]()

## Your First scGPT Application

The most common use case is generating cell embeddings from scRNA-seq data using a pretrained model. This requires three steps: loading data, loading a pretrained model, and generating embeddings.

### Step 1: Prepare Your Data

scGPT expects data in AnnData format, commonly used in single-cell analysis:

```python
import scanpy as sc

# Load your single-cell data
adata = sc.read_h5ad("your_data.h5ad")

# Basic preprocessing
sc.pp.filter_cells(adata, min_genes=200)
sc.pp.filter_genes(adata, min_cells=3)
```

### Step 2: Load Pretrained Model and Vocabulary

```python
import torch
from scgpt.model import TransformerModel
from scgpt.tokenizer import GeneVocab
from scgpt.utils import load_pretrained

# Load gene vocabulary
vocab = GeneVocab.from_file("vocab.json")

# Initialize model architecture
model = TransformerModel(
    ntoken=len(vocab),
    d_model=512,
    nhead=8,
    d_hid=512,
    nlayers=12,
    vocab=vocab,
    pad_token=vocab["<pad>"],
    pad_value=0,
)

# Load pretrained weights
load_pretrained(model, torch.load("best_model.pt", map_location="cpu"))
model.eval()
```

### Step 3: Generate Cell Embeddings

```python
from scgpt.tasks.cell_emb import embed_data

# Generate embeddings
adata = embed_data(
    model=model,
    adata=adata,
    gene_ids=adata.var.index.tolist(),
    batch_size=64,
    return_new_adata=True,
)

# Embeddings stored in adata.obsm['X_scGPT']
print(adata.obsm['X_scGPT'].shape)  # (n_cells, d_model)
```

**Sources:** [README.md:56-69](), [README.md:18]()

---

## Basic Usage Workflow: From Data to Embeddings

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "User Input"
        RAWDATA["AnnData Object<br/>adata.h5ad"]
        CKPT["Pretrained Checkpoint<br/>best_model.pt"]
        VOCAB["Gene Vocabulary<br/>vocab.json"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Loading Phase"
        VOCAB --> GENEVOCAB["GeneVocab.from_file()<br/>scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py"]
        GENEVOCAB --> VOCABOBJ["GeneVocab object<br/>gene_name to id mapping"]
        
        CKPT --> LOADPRETRAINED["load_pretrained()<br/>scgpt/utils/util.py:304"]
        VOCABOBJ --> TRANSMODEL["TransformerModel<br/>scgpt/model/model.py"]
        LOADPRETRAINED --> TRANSMODEL
        TRANSMODEL --> LOADEDMODEL["Loaded Model<br/>model.eval()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Inference Phase"
        RAWDATA --> EMBEDDATA["embed_data()<br/>scgpt/tasks/cell_emb.py"]
        LOADEDMODEL --> EMBEDDATA
        EMBEDDATA --> FORWARD["model.encode_batch()<br/>No gradient computation"]
        FORWARD --> CELLEMB["Cell Embeddings<br/>adata.obsm['X_scGPT']"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Downstream Applications"
        CELLEMB --> REFMAP["Reference Mapping<br/>tutorials/Tutorial_Reference_Mapping.ipynb"]
        CELLEMB --> INTEGRATION["Batch Integration<br/>tutorials/zero-shot/"]
        CELLEMB --> ANNOTATION["Cell Type Annotation<br/>Fine-tuning"]
    end
```

This diagram maps the typical zero-shot workflow to specific code entities. The `embed_data()` function in [scgpt/tasks/cell_emb.py]() is the primary interface for generating embeddings, while `load_pretrained()` in [scgpt/utils/util.py:304]() handles checkpoint loading across different backends (CPU, GPU, flash-attn).

**Sources:** [README.md:18](), [README.md:56-69]()

---

## Pretrained Model Zoo

scGPT provides several pretrained models for different use cases:

| Model Name | Training Data | Download Link | Use Case |
|------------|---------------|---------------|----------|
| **whole-human** | 33M normal human cells | [Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1oWh_-ZRdhtoGQ2Fw24HP41FgLoomVo-y) | **Recommended default** |
| **continual pretrained** | Continual pretraining on diverse batches | [Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1_GROJTzXiAV8HB4imruOTk6PEGuNOcgB) | Zero-shot embedding tasks |
| **brain** | 13.2M brain cells | [Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1vf1ijfQSk7rGdDGpBntR5bi5g6gNt-Gx) | Brain-specific analysis |
| **blood** | 10.3M blood/bone marrow cells | [Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1kkug5C7NjvXIwQGGaGoqXTk_Lb_pDrBU) | Hematology studies |
| **pan-cancer** | 5.7M cancer cells | [Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/13QzLHilYUd0v3HTwa_9n4G4yEF-hdkqa) | Cancer research |

Each checkpoint folder contains:
- `best_model.pt`: Model weights
- `vocab.json`: Gene vocabulary mapping gene names to token IDs
- `args.json`: Training configuration

**Note:** The `whole-human` model is recommended as the default starting point for most applications. Organ-specific models may provide competitive performance when the fine-tuning dataset shares similar cell type context with the training data.

**Sources:** [README.md:56-69]()

## Model Loading Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Checkpoint Files"
        CKPT["best_model.pt<br/>state_dict"]
        VOCAB_FILE["vocab.json<br/>gene mappings"]
        ARGS["args.json<br/>hyperparameters"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Vocabulary System"
        VOCAB_FILE --> GENEVOCAB_CLASS["GeneVocab class<br/>scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py"]
        GENEVOCAB_CLASS --> VOCAB_INSTANCE["vocab object<br/>len(vocab) = ntoken"]
        VOCAB_INSTANCE --> SPECIAL_TOKENS["Special tokens:<br/>&lt;pad&gt;, &lt;cls&gt;, &lt;eoc&gt;"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Initialization"
        VOCAB_INSTANCE --> TRANSMODEL_INIT["TransformerModel.__init__()<br/>scgpt/model/model.py"]
        ARGS --> TRANSMODEL_INIT
        
        TRANSMODEL_INIT --> GENE_ENCODER["GeneEncoder<br/>Embedding layer"]
        TRANSMODEL_INIT --> VALUE_ENCODER["ContinuousValueEncoder<br/>Expression values"]
        TRANSMODEL_INIT --> TRANSFORMER["TransformerEncoder<br/>12 layers default"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Weight Loading"
        CKPT --> TORCH_LOAD["torch.load()<br/>map_location"]
        TORCH_LOAD --> LOAD_PRETRAINED["load_pretrained()<br/>scgpt/utils/util.py:304"]
        LOAD_PRETRAINED --> CHECK_BACKEND["Check attention backend:<br/>FlashAttention vs Standard"]
        CHECK_BACKEND --> STATE_DICT["model.load_state_dict()"]
    end
    
    TRANSMODEL_INIT --> LOAD_PRETRAINED
    STATE_DICT --> READY_MODEL["model.eval()<br/>Ready for inference"]
    
    READY_MODEL --> EMBED_DATA_FUNC["embed_data()<br/>scgpt/tasks/cell_emb.py:258"]
```

The `load_pretrained()` function at [scgpt/utils/util.py:304]() handles automatic compatibility across different attention backends (flash-attn, standard PyTorch). This allows the same checkpoint to be loaded on CPU, GPU with flash-attention, or GPU with standard attention without modification.

**Sources:** [README.md:18](), [scgpt/data_collator.py:1-203]()

---

## Data Collation for Model Input

Once a model is loaded, raw AnnData needs to be converted into model-compatible batches. The `DataCollator` class handles this transformation:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Input Data Structure"
        EXAMPLE["Example dict:<br/>{{'id': tensor,<br/>'genes': tensor[gene_ids],<br/>'expressions': tensor[values]}}"]
    end
    
    subgraph "DataCollator Processing"
        EXAMPLE --> COLLATOR["DataCollator<br/>scgpt/data_collator.py"]
        
        COLLATOR --> BINNING["Value Binning<br/>binning(row, n_bins=51)<br/>scgpt/preprocess.py"]
        BINNING --> SAMPLE_TRUNC["Sample/Truncate<br/>max_length limit"]
        SAMPLE_TRUNC --> PADDING["Padding<br/>pad_token_id, pad_value"]
        PADDING --> MASKING["MLM Masking<br/>mlm_probability=0.15"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Tensors"
        MASKING --> OUTPUT["Batch dict:<br/>{{'gene': padded_genes,<br/>'expr': padded_expressions,<br/>'masked_expr': masked_expr}}"]
    end
    
    OUTPUT --> DATALOADER["DataLoader<br/>Batch iterator"]
    DATALOADER --> MODEL_INPUT["Model forward pass"]
```

The `DataCollator` parameters:
- `do_padding=True`: Pad sequences to `max_length`
- `pad_token_id`: Token ID for padding (typically vocab["<pad>"])
- `do_mlm=True`: Apply masked language modeling
- `mlm_probability=0.15`: Fraction of tokens to mask
- `do_binning=True`: Discretize expression values into 51 bins
- `sampling=True`: Randomly sample genes if length > max_length

**Sources:** [scgpt/data_collator.py:10-203]()

# Page: Installation

# Installation Guide

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [poetry.lock](poetry.lock)
- [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml)

</details>



This guide provides detailed instructions for installing and configuring scGPT, a foundation model for single-cell multi-omics data analysis. For information about the overall system architecture and components, see [Core Components](#2).

## Prerequisites

Before installing scGPT, ensure your system meets the following requirements:

- **Python**: Version ≥ 3.7.13
- **R**: Version ≥ 3.6.1 (for certain functionalities)
- **Hardware**: 
  - For CPU-only installation: Modern multi-core CPU with at least 16GB RAM
  - For GPU installation (recommended): CUDA-compatible GPU with at least 12GB VRAM

Sources: [README.md:29-30]()

## Installation Options

There are two primary methods to install scGPT: via pip (for users) or via Poetry (for developers).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["Start Installation"] --> Method{"Choose\nInstallation Method"}
    Method -->|"For Users"| PipMethod["pip install"]
    Method -->|"For Developers"| DevMethod["Poetry install"]
    
    PipMethod --> BasicPip["pip install scgpt"]
    BasicPip --> GPUSupport{"Need GPU\nAcceleration?"}
    
    GPUSupport -->|"Yes"| FlashAttn["Install flash-attn"]
    GPUSupport -->|"No"| Complete1["Installation Complete"]
    FlashAttn --> Complete2["Installation Complete"]
    
    DevMethod --> GitClone["git clone repository"]
    GitClone --> CDRepo["cd scGPT"]
    CDRepo --> PoetryInstall["poetry install"]
    PoetryInstall --> Complete3["Installation Complete"]
```

Sources: [README.md:28-52]()

## Basic Installation (pip)

The simplest method to install scGPT is via pip:

```bash
pip install scgpt
```

For optimal performance with GPU acceleration, install with flash-attention:

```bash
pip install scgpt "flash-attn<1.0.5"
```

**Note on compatibility:** If you encounter issues with the Google orbax package, use:

```bash
pip install scgpt "flash-attn<1.0.5" "orbax<0.1.8"
```

Optional: For logging and visualization capabilities, install wandb:

```bash
pip install wandb
```

Sources: [README.md:32-44]()

## Developer Installation (Poetry)

For developers contributing to scGPT, we recommend using Poetry for package management:

1. First, install Poetry following the instructions at [python-poetry.org](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation)

2. Clone the repository and install dependencies:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bowang-lab/scGPT
cd scGPT
poetry install
```

This will create a virtual environment with all dependencies specified in `pyproject.toml`.

Sources: [README.md:46-52](), [pyproject.toml:1-40]()

## Dependency Structure

scGPT relies on several key packages to function properly:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    scGPT["scGPT"] --> Core["Core Dependencies"]
    scGPT --> Optional["Optional Dependencies"]
    
    Core --> ML["Machine Learning"]
    Core --> SC["Single-Cell Analysis"]
    Core --> Utils["Utilities"]
    
    ML --> Torch["torch >=1.13.0"]
    ML --> Torchtext["torchtext"]
    
    SC --> Scanpy["scanpy ^1.9.1"]
    SC --> SCVI["scvi-tools >=0.16.0,<1.0"]
    SC --> SCIB["scib ^1.0.3"]
    
    Utils --> Pandas["pandas >=1.3.5"]
    Utils --> Numba["numba >=0.55.1"]
    Utils --> Datasets["datasets ^2.3.0"]
    
    Optional --> FlashAttn["flash-attn <1.0.5"]
    Optional --> WandB["wandb"]
```

Sources: [pyproject.toml:11-26](), [README.md:32-44]()

## GPU and CUDA Configuration

### CUDA Version Compatibility

For optimal performance, we recommend using:
- CUDA version 11.7
- flash-attn < 1.0.5

This combination has been tested and known to work well with scGPT.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CUDA["CUDA Runtime"] --> FA["flash-attention Library"]
    FA --> Torch["PyTorch"]
    Torch --> scGPT["scGPT"]
    
    subgraph "Recommended Versions"
        RCV["CUDA: 11.7"]
        RFA["flash-attn: <1.0.5"]
        RTorch["torch: >=1.13.0"]
    end
```

### Flash Attention Installation

The `flash-attn` package provides significant speed improvements for transformer-based operations but requires specific GPU and CUDA versions. If you encounter issues installing flash-attention, please refer to the [flash-attention GitHub repository](https://github.com/HazyResearch/flash-attention/tree/main) for detailed installation instructions specific to your hardware.

Sources: [README.md:54-56]()

## Troubleshooting Common Issues

### Flash Attention Installation Failures

If you encounter errors installing flash-attention:

1. Verify your CUDA version matches the recommended version
2. Try installing an older version of flash-attention:
   ```bash
   pip install "flash-attn==1.0.4"
   ```
3. If still unsuccessful, you can use scGPT without flash-attention (with reduced performance)

### Orbax Package Conflicts

If you see dependency conflicts with the orbax package:

```bash
pip install "orbax<0.1.8"
```

### Package Compatibility

scGPT's dependencies have specific version requirements. The table below shows key packages and their required versions:

| Package | Version Requirement |
|---------|---------------------|
| Python | >=3.7.12, <4 |
| pandas | >=1.3.5 |
| scvi-tools | >=0.16.0, <1.0 |
| scanpy | ^1.9.1 |
| torch | >=1.13.0 |
| numba | >=0.55.1 |
| datasets | ^2.3.0 |

Sources: [pyproject.toml:11-26](), [README.md:36-38]()

## Backend Support

As of version 0.2.4, scGPT's pretrained weights can be loaded on multiple backends:

- PyTorch CPU
- PyTorch GPU
- flash-attention

This flexibility allows users to use the model with or without specialized hardware acceleration.

The pretrained weights can be loaded using the `load_pretrained` function:

```python
from scgpt.utils.util import load_pretrained
import torch

# Load model
target_model = YourModel()  # Your initialized model
load_pretrained(target_model, torch.load("path_to_checkpoint.pt"))
```

Sources: [README.md:18]()

## Verifying Your Installation

After installation, you can verify that scGPT is correctly installed by running:

```python
import scgpt
print(scgpt.__version__)  # Should print the installed version
```

For further verification, try loading one of the models:

```python
from scgpt.utils.util import load_pretrained
from scgpt.models.model import TransformerModel
import torch

# Initialize a small model just to test
model = TransformerModel(
    ntoken=100,  # placeholder
    d_model=128,
    nhead=4,
    d_hid=512,
    nlayers=2,
)

# This should run without errors if installation is correct
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
model = model.to(device)
```

# Page: Quick Start with Pretrained Models

# Quick Start with Pretrained Models

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [scgpt/data_collator.py](scgpt/data_collator.py)
- [tutorials/zero-shot/Tutorial_ZeroShot_Integration.ipynb](tutorials/zero-shot/Tutorial_ZeroShot_Integration.ipynb)
- [tutorials/zero-shot/Tutorial_ZeroShot_Integration_Continual_Pretraining.ipynb](tutorials/zero-shot/Tutorial_ZeroShot_Integration_Continual_Pretraining.ipynb)
- [tutorials/zero-shot/Tutorial_ZeroShot_Reference_Mapping.ipynb](tutorials/zero-shot/Tutorial_ZeroShot_Reference_Mapping.ipynb)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This guide shows how to quickly load and use scGPT's pretrained models for common single-cell analysis tasks without any fine-tuning or training. These models provide out-of-the-box cell embeddings that can be used for tasks like reference mapping, data integration, and cell annotation.

For information about fine-tuning pretrained models for specific downstream tasks, see [Fine-tuning Applications](#6). For details on the model architecture itself, see [Model Architecture](#3.1).

## Available Pretrained Models

scGPT provides several pretrained checkpoints optimized for different biological contexts:

| Model Name | Description | Training Data | Primary Use Cases | Download Link |
|------------|-------------|---------------|-------------------|---------------|
| `whole-human` (recommended) | General-purpose human model | 33M normal human cells | Default choice for most applications | [Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1oWh_-ZRdhtoGQ2Fw24HP41FgLoomVo-y?usp=sharing) |
| `continual pretrained` (scGPT_CP) | Enhanced for zero-shot tasks | Tabula Sapiens with cell type supervision | Cell embedding tasks with batch effects | [Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1_GROJTzXiAV8HB4imruOTk6PEGuNOcgB?usp=sharing) |
| `brain` | Brain tissue specialist | 13.2M brain cells | Brain-specific analyses | [Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1vf1ijfQSk7rGdDGpBntR5bi5g6gNt-Gx?usp=sharing) |
| `blood` | Blood/bone marrow specialist | 10.3M blood and bone marrow cells | Hematological analyses | [Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1kkug5C7NjvXIwQGGaGoqXTk_Lb_pDrBU?usp=sharing) |
| `heart` | Heart tissue specialist | 1.8M heart cells | Cardiac analyses | [Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1GcgXrd7apn6y4Ze_iSCncskX3UsWPY2r?usp=sharing) |
| `lung` | Lung tissue specialist | 2.1M lung cells | Pulmonary analyses | [Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/16A1DJ30PT6bodt4bWLa4hpS7gbWZQFBG?usp=sharing) |
| `kidney` | Kidney tissue specialist | 814K kidney cells | Renal analyses | [Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1S-1AR65DF120kNFpEbWCvRHPhpkGK3kK?usp=sharing) |
| `pan-cancer` | Cancer specialist | 5.7M cancer cells | Cancer/tumor analyses | [Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/13QzLHilYUd0v3HTwa_9n4G4yEF-hdkqa?usp=sharing) |

The `whole-human` model is recommended as the default starting point. The `scGPT_CP` (continual pretrained) model offers improved performance on datasets with observable technical batch effects, especially for zero-shot integration and reference mapping tasks.

**Sources:** [README.md:56-69]()

## Model Checkpoint Structure

Each pretrained model checkpoint folder contains two essential files:

```
model_directory/
├── vocab.json          # Gene vocabulary mapping gene names to token IDs
└── best_model.pt       # Model weights and configuration
```

The `vocab.json` file maps gene names (or ENSEMBL IDs) to integer token IDs used by the model. The vocabulary size for the whole-human model is 60,697 genes. The `best_model.pt` file contains the trained TransformerModel weights and can be loaded on CPU, GPU, or flash-attention backends.

**Sources:** [README.md:58](), [tutorials/zero-shot/Tutorial_ZeroShot_Reference_Mapping.ipynb:20]()

## Basic Usage Workflow

The typical workflow for using a pretrained model consists of four steps:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Load AnnData object<br/>(raw counts)"] --> B["Preprocess data<br/>normalize, HVG selection"]
    B --> C["Generate embeddings<br/>scg.tasks.embed_data()"]
    C --> D["Use embeddings<br/>integration, mapping, annotation"]
    
    E["Download model checkpoint<br/>vocab.json + best_model.pt"] --> C
    
    style C fill:#f9f9f9
    style E fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Workflow Diagram: Pretrained Model Usage Pipeline**

The core function for using pretrained models is `scg.tasks.embed_data()`, which takes your preprocessed data and a model directory, then returns cell embeddings stored in `adata.obsm['X_scGPT']`.

**Sources:** [tutorials/zero-shot/Tutorial_ZeroShot_Reference_Mapping.ipynb:23-29](), [tutorials/zero-shot/Tutorial_ZeroShot_Integration.ipynb:28-32]()

## Using embed_data Function

### Function Overview

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["AnnData<br/>gene expression"] --> ED["scg.tasks.embed_data()"]
    Model["model_dir<br/>checkpoint folder"] --> ED
    ED --> Output["AnnData<br/>with X_scGPT embeddings"]
    
    Params["Parameters:<br/>gene_col<br/>batch_size<br/>obs_to_save<br/>device"] -.-> ED
```

**Diagram: embed_data Function Interface**

The `embed_data` function is the primary interface for generating cell embeddings from pretrained models. It performs a forward pass through the model without computing gradients.

### Function Signature

```python
scg.tasks.embed_data(
    adata: AnnData,
    model_dir: Path,
    gene_col: str = "gene_name",
    batch_size: int = 64,
    obs_to_save: List[str] = None,
    device: str = "cuda",
    use_fast_transformer: bool = True,
    return_new_adata: bool = False
) -> AnnData
```

### Input Requirements

| Parameter | Type | Description | Example |
|-----------|------|-------------|---------|
| `adata` | `AnnData` | Preprocessed single-cell data with gene expression matrix | `sc.read_h5ad('data.h5ad')` |
| `model_dir` | `Path` | Directory containing `vocab.json` and `best_model.pt` | `Path("save/scGPT_human")` |
| `gene_col` | `str` | Column in `adata.var` containing gene names/symbols | `"gene_name"` or `"gene_symbols"` |
| `batch_size` | `int` | Number of cells to process per batch | `64` |
| `device` | `str` | Computation device | `"cuda"` or `"cpu"` |

The input `adata` should contain:
- **X matrix**: Gene expression values (normalized or log-normalized)
- **var**: Gene metadata with column specified by `gene_col`
- **obs**: Cell metadata (optional, preserved in output)

### Data Preprocessing Requirements

Before calling `embed_data`, your data should be preprocessed:

```python
import scanpy as sc

# Load data
adata = sc.read_h5ad('your_data.h5ad')

# Basic preprocessing
sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum=1e4)
sc.pp.log1p(adata)

# Select highly variable genes (recommended)
sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(adata, n_top_genes=3000, flavor='seurat_v3')
adata = adata[:, adata.var['highly_variable']]

# Ensure gene names are in var
adata.var['gene_name'] = adata.var.index.values
```

The model will match genes in your data against its vocabulary. Unmatched genes are excluded from processing.

**Sources:** [tutorials/zero-shot/Tutorial_ZeroShot_Integration.ipynb:212-218](), [tutorials/zero-shot/Tutorial_ZeroShot_Reference_Mapping.ipynb:155-160]()

### Output Format

The function returns an `AnnData` object with embeddings stored in `adata.obsm['X_scGPT']`:

```python
# Generate embeddings
embed_adata = scg.tasks.embed_data(
    adata,
    model_dir=Path("save/scGPT_human"),
    gene_col="gene_name",
    batch_size=64,
)

# Access embeddings
embeddings = embed_adata.obsm['X_scGPT']  # Shape: (n_cells, embedding_dim)
```

The embedding dimension is typically 512 for the standard model. The output preserves all original cell metadata from `adata.obs`.

**Sources:** [tutorials/zero-shot/Tutorial_ZeroShot_Reference_Mapping.ipynb:191-196](), [tutorials/zero-shot/Tutorial_ZeroShot_Integration.ipynb:324-329]()

## Complete Example

### Reference Mapping Example

```python
from pathlib import Path
import scanpy as sc
import scgpt as scg

# 1. Specify model directory
model_dir = Path("save/scGPT_human")

# 2. Load and preprocess reference data
adata = sc.read_h5ad('data/reference.h5ad')
sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(adata, n_top_genes=3000, flavor='seurat_v3')
adata = adata[:, adata.var['highly_variable']]

# Set gene column name
gene_col = "gene_name"
adata.var[gene_col] = adata.var.index.values

# 3. Generate embeddings
ref_embed_adata = scg.tasks.embed_data(
    adata,
    model_dir,
    gene_col=gene_col,
    batch_size=64,
)

# 4. Load and embed query data
test_adata = sc.read_h5ad('data/query.h5ad')
test_adata = test_adata[:, test_adata.var[gene_col].isin(adata.var[gene_col])]

test_embed_adata = scg.tasks.embed_data(
    test_adata,
    model_dir,
    gene_col=gene_col,
    batch_size=64,
)

# 5. Use embeddings for downstream analysis
# Embeddings are in: ref_embed_adata.obsm['X_scGPT']
#                    test_embed_adata.obsm['X_scGPT']
```

**Sources:** [tutorials/zero-shot/Tutorial_ZeroShot_Reference_Mapping.ipynb:155-233]()

### Integration Example

```python
from pathlib import Path
import scanpy as sc
import scgpt as scg

# 1. Specify model directory (using continual pretrained model)
model_dir = Path("save/scGPT_CP")

# 2. Load and preprocess data with multiple batches
adata = sc.read_h5ad('data/integration_data.h5ad')

# Preprocess
sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum=1e4)
sc.pp.log1p(adata)
sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(adata, n_top_genes=1800, flavor='seurat_v3')
adata = adata[:, adata.var['highly_variable']]

# Set gene column
gene_col = "gene_name"
batch_key = "batch"
cell_type_key = "celltype"

# 3. Generate embeddings
embed_adata = scg.tasks.embed_data(
    adata,
    model_dir,
    gene_col=gene_col,
    batch_size=64,
)

# 4. Use embeddings for integration analysis
# The X_scGPT embeddings naturally integrate across batches
sc.pp.neighbors(embed_adata, use_rep='X_scGPT')
sc.tl.umap(embed_adata)
sc.pl.umap(embed_adata, color=[batch_key, cell_type_key])
```

**Sources:** [tutorials/zero-shot/Tutorial_ZeroShot_Integration_Continual_Pretraining.ipynb:239-329]()

## Model Loading Details

### Backend Compatibility

The pretrained models can be loaded on different computational backends:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CP["Checkpoint Files<br/>vocab.json + best_model.pt"] --> LF["load_pretrained()<br/>utils.util:304"]
    
    LF --> CPU["CPU Backend<br/>No special requirements"]
    LF --> GPU["GPU Backend<br/>Standard CUDA"]
    LF --> FLASH["Flash-Attention Backend<br/>flash-attn &lt; 1.0.5"]
    
    CPU --> Model["TransformerModel"]
    GPU --> Model
    FLASH --> Model
```

**Diagram: Model Loading Backend Options**

The `load_pretrained` function handles loading model weights onto the appropriate backend. Flash-attention is optional but recommended for improved performance on compatible GPUs.

```python
import torch
from scgpt.model import TransformerModel
from scgpt.utils import load_pretrained

# Load model
model = TransformerModel(...)
load_pretrained(model, torch.load("path/to/best_model.pt"))
```

**Sources:** [README.md:18](), [scgpt/utils/util.py:304]()

### Vocabulary Matching

When generating embeddings, the model matches genes in your data against its vocabulary:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["Input Genes<br/>adata.var[gene_col]"] --> Match["Gene Matching<br/>tasks/cell_emb.py:213"]
    Vocab["vocab.json<br/>60,697 genes"] --> Match
    Match --> Matched["Matched Genes<br/>processed by model"]
    Match --> Unmatched["Unmatched Genes<br/>excluded"]
    
    Matched --> Embed["Gene Embeddings<br/>GeneEncoder"]
```

**Diagram: Gene Vocabulary Matching Process**

The system reports how many genes were successfully matched. For example:
```
scGPT - INFO - match 2978/3000 genes in vocabulary of size 60697.
```

Only matched genes are used for generating cell embeddings. Genes not in the vocabulary are silently excluded.

**Sources:** [tutorials/zero-shot/Tutorial_ZeroShot_Integration.ipynb:332-336](), [scgpt/data_collator.py:1-203]()

## Data Collation Process

Internally, `embed_data` uses a `DataCollator` to prepare batches:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Raw["Raw Gene Expression"] --> Bin["Expression Binning<br/>51 bins"]
    Bin --> Pad["Padding/Truncation<br/>to max_length"]
    Pad --> Batch["Batched Tensors<br/>gene IDs + expression"]
    Batch --> Forward["Model Forward Pass<br/>no gradients"]
    Forward --> Emb["Cell Embeddings"]
    
    Params["DataCollator params:<br/>pad_token_id<br/>max_length<br/>do_binning"] -.-> Pad
```

**Diagram: Data Collation Pipeline**

Key data collation features:
- **Expression binning**: Continuous expression values are discretized into 51 bins
- **Padding**: Sequences are padded to consistent length with `pad_token_id`
- **Sampling**: For sequences exceeding `max_length`, genes are randomly sampled
- **No masking**: Unlike training, no MLM masking is applied during inference

**Sources:** [scgpt/data_collator.py:11-203]()

## Tips and Best Practices

### Model Selection Guidelines

| Your Data Characteristics | Recommended Model |
|---------------------------|-------------------|
| General human single-cell data | `whole-human` |
| Multiple batches with technical effects | `scGPT_CP` (continual pretrained) |
| Brain-specific tissue | `brain` (if context matches training data) |
| Blood/immune cells | `blood` (if context matches training data) |
| Other specific organs | Corresponding organ model if available |
| Cancer/tumor samples | `pan-cancer` |

### Gene Selection

- Select 1,800-3,000 highly variable genes for optimal performance
- More genes provide more information but increase computation time
- Use `flavor='seurat_v3'` for HVG selection for consistency with training

### Batch Size

- Larger batch sizes (64-128) are faster but require more memory
- Reduce batch size if encountering out-of-memory errors
- Batch size does not affect embedding quality

### Preprocessing Consistency

- Normalize and log-transform consistently with training data
- Target sum of 1e4 (10,000) is standard
- HVG selection should use raw counts when `flavor='seurat_v3'`

**Sources:** [tutorials/zero-shot/Tutorial_ZeroShot_Integration.ipynb:135-303](), [README.md:56-72]()

## Next Steps

After generating embeddings with pretrained models:

- **For zero-shot reference mapping**: See [Reference Mapping](#4.1)
- **For zero-shot data integration**: See [Data Integration](#4.2)  
- **For fine-tuning on specific tasks**: See [Cell Type Annotation](#6.1), [Perturbation Prediction](#6.2), or other fine-tuning guides
- **For understanding the embedding space**: See [Cell Embedding System](#5)

**Sources:** [README.md:1-114]()

# Page: Core Architecture

# Core Architecture

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [scgpt/data_collator.py](scgpt/data_collator.py)
- [scgpt/model/generation_model.py](scgpt/model/generation_model.py)
- [scgpt/model/model.py](scgpt/model/model.py)
- [scgpt/utils/util.py](scgpt/utils/util.py)

</details>



This page provides an architectural overview of the scGPT system, explaining the fundamental components and subsystems that enable scGPT's functionality as a foundation model for single-cell genomics. The architecture is organized into three primary subsystems: the model layer, the data processing pipeline, and the training infrastructure.

For detailed information about specific subsystems, refer to the following subpages:
- **[Model Architecture (3.1)](#3.1)** - Detailed explanation of TransformerModel and TransformerGenerator architectures, including encoders, decoders, and attention mechanisms
- **[Tokenization and Vocabulary (3.2)](#3.2)** - GeneVocab system, tokenization process, and special token handling
- **[Data Processing Pipeline (3.3)](#3.3)** - Preprocessor, DataCollator, and data preparation workflow from raw data to model input
- **[Training Infrastructure (3.4)](#3.4)** - Training loop, loss functions, evaluation metrics, and optimizer configuration

## Architectural Overview

scGPT is organized around three primary subsystems that work together to enable single-cell genomics modeling:

1. **Model Layer** - Transformer-based neural network architectures (`TransformerModel`, `TransformerGenerator`)
2. **Data Processing Pipeline** - Tokenization, preprocessing, and batch collation (`GeneVocab`, `Preprocessor`, `DataCollator`)
3. **Training Infrastructure** - Training loop, loss functions, and evaluation (`Trainer`, multi-objective losses)

**High-Level Architecture Diagram**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Data Processing Pipeline"
        RAW["Raw scRNA-seq Data<br/>(AnnData)"]
        PREPROC["Preprocessor<br/>Filter, Normalize, HVG"]
        VOCAB["GeneVocab<br/>Tokenization"]
        DATACOL["DataCollator<br/>Padding, Masking"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Layer"
        TM["TransformerModel<br/>scgpt/model/model.py"]
        TG["TransformerGenerator<br/>scgpt/model/generation_model.py"]
        ENCODERS["Encoders<br/>Gene, Value, Batch"]
        TE["TransformerEncoder<br/>12 layers, 512 dim"]
        DECODERS["Decoders<br/>Expr, Cls, MVC, DAR"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Training Infrastructure"
        TRAINER["Trainer<br/>scgpt/trainer.py"]
        LOSS["Loss Functions<br/>GEP, CLS, MVC, DAR, ECS"]
        EVAL["Evaluation Metrics"]
    end
    
    RAW --> PREPROC
    PREPROC --> VOCAB
    VOCAB --> DATACOL
    DATACOL --> TRAINER
    
    TRAINER --> TM
    TRAINER --> TG
    TM --> ENCODERS
    ENCODERS --> TE
    TE --> DECODERS
    
    TRAINER --> LOSS
    LOSS --> EVAL
    
    TM --> CELLEMB["Cell Embeddings<br/>X_scGPT"]
    TG --> PERTPRED["Perturbation Predictions"]
```

Sources: [scgpt/__init__.py:18-29](), [scgpt/model/model.py:28-168](), [scgpt/model/generation_model.py:25-125](), [scgpt/data_collator.py:10-66]()

## Model Layer

The model layer contains the core neural network architectures that perform single-cell genomics modeling. scGPT provides two transformer-based models, each designed for different use cases. For detailed architecture information, see **[Model Architecture (3.1)](#3.1)**.

**Model Hierarchy**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "scgpt/model/model.py"
        TM["TransformerModel<br/>General Purpose Model"]
        TM_ENC["Encoders:<br/>GeneEncoder<br/>ContinuousValueEncoder<br/>BatchLabelEncoder"]
        TM_TRANS["TransformerEncoder<br/>12 layers default"]
        TM_DEC["Decoders:<br/>ExprDecoder (GEP)<br/>ClsDecoder (CLS)<br/>MVCDecoder (MVC)<br/>AdversarialDiscriminator (DAR)"]
        
        TM --> TM_ENC
        TM_ENC --> TM_TRANS
        TM_TRANS --> TM_DEC
    end
    
    subgraph "scgpt/model/generation_model.py"
        TG["TransformerGenerator<br/>Perturbation Prediction Model"]
        TG_ENC["Encoders:<br/>GeneEncoder<br/>ContinuousValueEncoder<br/>PerturbationEncoder"]
        TG_TRANS["TransformerEncoder<br/>12 layers default"]
        TG_DEC["Decoder:<br/>AffineExprDecoder<br/>(Coefficient + Bias)"]
        
        TG --> TG_ENC
        TG_ENC --> TG_TRANS
        TG_TRANS --> TG_DEC
    end
    
    PRETRAIN["Pretrained Checkpoints<br/>scGPT_human (60,697 genes)<br/>scGPT_CP<br/>Organ-specific models"] -.->|"load_pretrained()"| TM
    PRETRAIN -.->|"load_pretrained()"| TG
```

| Model | File | Primary Use Cases | Key Features |
|-------|------|-------------------|--------------|
| `TransformerModel` | [scgpt/model/model.py:28-442]() | Cell embedding, integration, annotation | Multi-objective training (GEP, CLS, MVC, DAR, ECS) |
| `TransformerGenerator` | [scgpt/model/generation_model.py:25-350]() | Perturbation prediction | Affine expression decoder, perturbation encoding |

**Key Architecture Features:**
- **Flash Attention Support**: Optional use of `FlashMHA` for memory-efficient attention ([scgpt/model/model.py:115-129]())
- **Domain-Specific Batch Normalization**: Handles batch effects during training ([scgpt/model/model.py:105-113]())
- **Flexible Cell Embedding Extraction**: Supports `cls`, `avg-pool`, and `w-pool` strategies ([scgpt/model/model.py:199-223]())
- **Explicit Zero-Inflation Modeling**: Models dropout events in single-cell data ([scgpt/model/model.py:364-370]())

Sources: [scgpt/model/model.py:28-442](), [scgpt/model/generation_model.py:25-350](), [scgpt/utils/util.py:308-365]()

## Data Processing Pipeline

The data processing pipeline transforms raw single-cell RNA-seq data into model-ready tensors. This pipeline consists of three stages: preprocessing, tokenization, and batch collation. For detailed information, see **[Data Processing Pipeline (3.3)](#3.3)** and **[Tokenization and Vocabulary (3.2)](#3.2)**.

**Data Flow Through Pipeline**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Input"
        ADATA["AnnData Object<br/>cells × genes matrix"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 1: Preprocessing"
        FILTER["Filter Cells/Genes"]
        NORM["Normalize<br/>(library size)"]
        HVG["Select HVGs<br/>(optional)"]
        BIN["Binning<br/>(n_bins=51)"]
        
        FILTER --> NORM
        NORM --> HVG
        HVG --> BIN
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 2: Tokenization"
        VOCAB["GeneVocab<br/>gene → token_id"]
        TOKEN["Create Tensors:<br/>gene_ids, values"]
        
        VOCAB --> TOKEN
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 3: Batch Collation"
        PAD["Padding<br/>(to max_length)"]
        MASK["MLM Masking<br/>(mlm_probability=0.15)"]
        BATCH["Batched Tensors"]
        
        PAD --> MASK
        MASK --> BATCH
    end
    
    ADATA --> FILTER
    BIN --> TOKEN
    TOKEN --> PAD
    BATCH --> MODEL["Model Input"]
```

| Component | File | Responsibility |
|-----------|------|----------------|
| `Preprocessor` | [scgpt/preprocess.py]() | Filter, normalize, HVG selection, binning |
| `GeneVocab` | [scgpt/tokenizer/gene_tokenizer.py]() | Maintain gene vocabulary, handle special tokens |
| `DataCollator` | [scgpt/data_collator.py:10-203]() | Pad sequences, apply masking, create batches |

**Key Data Structures:**

The pipeline produces the following data structures for model input:

```python
# Example batch structure from DataCollator
{
    "gene": torch.Tensor,      # shape: (batch_size, max_length), gene token IDs
    "expr": torch.Tensor,      # shape: (batch_size, max_length), expression values
    "masked_expr": torch.Tensor # shape: (batch_size, max_length), masked expression values
}
```

**Special Tokens:**

The vocabulary includes special tokens for model operations:
- `<pad>`: Padding token for variable-length sequences
- `<cls>`: Classification token prepended to sequences
- `<eoc>`: End-of-cell token (optional)

Sources: [scgpt/data_collator.py:10-203](), [scgpt/__init__.py:19-20]()

## Training Infrastructure

The training infrastructure orchestrates the training loop, manages multi-objective losses, and evaluates model performance. For detailed information, see **[Training Infrastructure (3.4)](#3.4)**.

**Training Loop Architecture**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant DATA as "DataLoader"
    participant TRAINER as "Trainer<br/>scgpt/trainer.py"
    participant MODEL as "TransformerModel"
    participant LOSS as "Loss Computation"
    participant OPT as "Optimizer<br/>AdamW"
    participant SCHED as "Scheduler"
    
    loop Each Epoch
        loop Each Batch
            DATA->>TRAINER: Batch data
            TRAINER->>MODEL: Forward pass
            MODEL->>LOSS: Model outputs
            Note over LOSS: Multi-objective:<br/>GEP + CLS + MVC + DAR + ECS
            LOSS->>TRAINER: Combined loss
            TRAINER->>OPT: Backward pass
            OPT->>MODEL: Update weights
            TRAINER->>SCHED: Step scheduler
        end
        TRAINER->>TRAINER: Evaluate on validation
        TRAINER->>TRAINER: Save checkpoint
    end
```

**Multi-Objective Training:**

scGPT supports multiple training objectives that can be combined:

| Objective | Name | Purpose | Loss Function |
|-----------|------|---------|---------------|
| GEP | Gene Expression Prediction | Masked language modeling for expression values | MSE Loss |
| CLS | Cell Type Classification | Supervised cell type prediction | Cross-Entropy Loss |
| MVC | Masked Value Prediction for Cell Embedding | Contrastive learning for cell representations | MSE Loss |
| DAR | Domain Adaptation via Reverse Gradient | Remove batch effects | Cross-Entropy Loss with gradient reversal |
| ECS | Elastic Cell Similarity | Regularize cell embeddings | Custom similarity loss |

**Forward Pass with Multiple Objectives:**

```python
# Example from TransformerModel.forward()
output = model(
    src=gene_ids,                # Gene token IDs
    values=gene_values,          # Expression values
    src_key_padding_mask=mask,   # Attention mask
    batch_labels=batch_ids,      # Batch information
    CLS=True,                    # Enable classification objective
    MVC=True,                    # Enable MVC objective
    ECS=True                     # Enable ECS objective
)
# Returns: {"mlm_output", "cell_emb", "cls_output", "mvc_output", "loss_ecs"}
```

Sources: [scgpt/model/model.py:314-440](), [scgpt/model/generation_model.py:175-262]()

## Configuration and Key Parameters

The scGPT architecture is highly configurable. Below are the most important configuration parameters for each subsystem:

**Model Architecture Parameters:**

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `ntoken` | - | Vocabulary size (number of genes) |
| `d_model` | 512 | Embedding dimension |
| `nhead` | 8 | Number of attention heads |
| `d_hid` | 512 | Hidden layer dimension in feedforward network |
| `nlayers` | 12 | Number of transformer encoder layers |
| `dropout` | 0.0 | Dropout probability |
| `use_fast_transformer` | True | Enable FlashAttention or linear attention |
| `cell_emb_style` | "cls" | Cell embedding extraction method: "cls", "avg-pool", or "w-pool" |
| `explicit_zero_prob` | False | Model zero-inflation with explicit probability |

**Data Processing Parameters:**

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `n_input_bins` | 51 | Number of bins for discretizing expression values |
| `mlm_probability` | 0.15 | Probability of masking gene tokens for MLM objective |
| `mask_value` | -1 | Value to fill masked positions |
| `max_length` | 1200-3000 | Maximum sequence length (varies by task) |
| `pad_token_id` | - | Token ID for padding |

**Training Parameters:**

| Parameter | Typical Value | Description |
|-----------|---------------|-------------|
| `learning_rate` | 1e-4 | Base learning rate |
| `batch_size` | 32-64 | Number of cells per batch |
| `epochs` | 10-30 | Number of training epochs |
| `warmup_ratio` | 0.1 | Fraction of training for learning rate warmup |

Sources: [scgpt/model/model.py:28-167](), [scgpt/model/generation_model.py:25-64](), [scgpt/data_collator.py:36-46]()

## Key Implementation Details

The scGPT models include several specialized implementation features:

1. **Flash Attention Support**: Optional use of flash attention for improved memory usage and speed
2. **Domain-Specific Batch Normalization**: Support for batch-aware normalization to handle domain shifts
3. **Multiple Cell Embedding Styles**: Options for how cell representations are derived from gene-level features
4. **Zero-Inflation Modeling**: Specialized components to model dropout events in single-cell data

Sources: [scgpt/model/model.py:64-84](), [scgpt/model/model.py:595-720]()
